description:
The provided image contains two line plots illustrating the relationship between variables over a sequence of steps, likely representing a compression or tokenization process in the context of the paper "SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator."

The top plot displays the variable `n_i` on the y-axis against the step index `i` on the x-axis. The y-axis is labeled `n_i` and ranges from 0 to `c - a`, with intermediate tick marks at `w` and `c - a - s`. The x-axis is labeled `i` and spans from 0 to `i_{max}`, with tick marks at 0 and `i_{max}`. The plot shows a piecewise linear function that starts at 0, increases linearly to `c - a`, then drops to `w`, and repeats this pattern of rising and falling in a sawtooth-like fashion until `i_{max}`. The line is solid and uses a triangular marker at the start of each segment.

The bottom plot displays the variable `Size_{run}` on the y-axis against the same step index `i` on the x-axis. The y-axis is labeled `Size_{run}` and ranges from 0 to `c`, with intermediate tick marks at `w + a + s` and `c`. The x-axis is identical to the top plot, labeled `i` and spanning from 0 to `i_{max}`. The plot shows a similar piecewise linear function, starting at 0, increasing linearly to `c`, then dropping to `w + a + s`, and repeating this pattern until `i_{max}`. The line is also solid and uses a triangular marker at the start of each segment.

Both plots share the same x-axis, indicating that they represent the same sequence of steps. The y-axis values in the bottom plot are consistently higher than those in the top plot, suggesting that `Size_{run}` represents a different or scaled metric than `n_i`. The sawtooth pattern in both plots indicates a periodic or cyclical behavior, likely corresponding to the compression or segmentation process described in the paper.
